title: Arbiters of Ambivalence: Challenges of Using LLMs in No-Consensus Tasks
findings: The paper does not offer findings specific to religion, but includes a religious question ('Were Adam and Eve real historical figures?') within its 'Controversial Questions' category. For this category, models showed a universal decrease in neutrality when acting as judges or debaters compared to when they were answer generators. LLMs are much more likely to take a stance on such topics in judge and debate modes, whereas they produce more nuanced and neutral outputs as answer generators.
